summary: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling

title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding
summary: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. title: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
summary: Despite the success of video world models, extending them to multiple agents is difficult because it requires generating several agent-specific video streams that are consistent in time and between agents. title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
summary: Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response. In this paper, we identify a fundamental limitation in this process, where models make substantially more errors when tasks are composed, even when they can solve every constituent task reliably in isolation. This degradation cannot be fully explained by the accumulation of independent errors.

title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
summary: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws. title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses. summary: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. summary: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. summary: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. summary: We prove that every $\operatorname{ReLU}$ network can be exactly simulated by a $\operatorname{ReLU}$ network with two hidden layers. We present two proofs: one that is based on fillings in homological algebra and a direct combinatorial proof.
